definition: Semantic folding theory describes a procedure for encoding the semantics of natural language text in a semantically grounded binary representation.
details: This approach provides a framework for modelling how language data is processed by the neocortex.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. Think of it this way: Semantic folding theory describes a procedure for encoding the semantics of natural language text in a semantically grounded binary representation. And here is the clever part: This approach provides a framework for modelling how language data is processed by the neocortex. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. And that is Semantic folding — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
